non_nvidia_amd_apple_gpu_training.vulkan: No peer documents LLM fine-tuning on Vulkan. Upstream llama.cpp's Vulkan backend DOES implement every op llama-finetune needs (OUT_PROD, SILU_BACK, RMS_NORM_BACK, SOFT_MAX_BACK, ROPE_BACK, CROSS_ENTROPY_LOSS(_BACK), OPT_STEP_ADAMW/SGD in ggml-vulkan.cpp supports_op ~L15558-15735), so full FP32 fine-tuning can run there at source level, but examples/training/README.md names only CPU and CUDA and calls the code WIP.
non_nvidia_amd_apple_gpu_training.webgpu: NO. llama.cpp's WebGPU backend supports none of the training ops (no OPT_STEP, OUT_PROD, CROSS_ENTROPY or *_BACK case in ggml-webgpu.cpp supports_op). No listed peer trains in a browser. GitHub search for WebGPU fine-tuning found only toy repos (largest: jsgrad-org/jsgrad, 63 stars, general ML, not LLM LoRA).

non_nvidia_amd_apple_gpu_training.verdict: Vendor-neutral (Vulkan) LLM LoRA training is NOT an empty lane: QVAC Fabric, a small llama.cpp fork, claims it on NVIDIA/AMD/Intel/Apple/Adreno/Mali with Q4/Q8 bases and publishes per-device epoch times. None of the 20 listed peers offers it. WebGPU / in-browser LLM fine-tuning appears unoccupied (no peer, no fork, no project over 100 stars found). Neither QVAC nor anyone else in this set claims cross-vendor bit-identical training or reports joules per training step.

Every have/partial carries a URL or repo path read this session (gh api repo contents/readme, unsloth.ai .md docs, HF docs via WebFetch). llama.cpp is scored on upstream master only; the QVAC Fabric fork is reported separately under answers.
